title: Tardigrades have survived exposure to the vacuum of open space
body: Tardigrades, or water bears, are eight-legged animals about half a millimetre long. When their surroundings dry out, many species shrivel into a dormant ‘tun’, losing most of their water and slowing their metabolism almost to a stop while protective proteins shield their cells. In 2007, dried tardigrades flew on the FOTON-M3 mission and spent 10 days exposed to open space. The vacuum alone had no significant effect on them.

slides.heading: Not invincible
slides.text: Active, water-filled tardigrades are far more fragile. Their famous toughness belongs mainly to the dried tun state, and it varies a lot between species.

slides.heading: Sunlight was the real test
slides.text: In the same experiment, adding unfiltered solar ultraviolet light killed many of the tuns, though some still revived when they were rehydrated back on Earth.

slides.heading: An ancient design
slides.text: Tardigrades are an old lineage. The earliest known tardigrade fossil dates from the Cambrian period, some 500 million years ago.
